laws.jurisdiction: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec (CAI)
laws.scope: Individuals in Quebec whose personal information is held by enterprises operating in Quebec
laws.applies_to: Private-sector enterprises carrying on an enterprise in Quebec (the Act's s.1), including those outside Quebec handling Quebec residents' data
laws.key_requirements: Consent that is clear, free and specific (s.14); rights of access, rectification, portability and de-indexation; privacy impact assessments for projects and cross-border transfers (s.3.3, 17); mandatory reporting of confidentiality incidents to CAI and individuals (s.3.5); designated person in charge of personal information (s.3.1)
laws.data_categories: Personal information; sensitive information (medical; biometric or otherwise intimate; s.12)
laws.retention_period: Keep only as long as necessary for the purposes; then destroy or anonymize (s.23)

laws.research_exemption: Information may be released without consent for study or research purposes after a privacy impact assessment and written agreement (s.21-21.0.2)
laws.genetic_data: No specific genetic rule; falls under sensitive information (medical or intimate) requiring express consent (s.12, 12 para 2) (unconfirmed)

laws.scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
laws.applies_to: Persons doing business in NE that process personal data and are not small businesses under the federal Small Business Act; small businesses may not sell sensitive data without consent
laws.key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments; 30-day cure period (does not sunset)
laws.enforcement_authority: Nebraska Attorney General
laws.penalties_range: Up to USD 7,500 per violation not cured within 30 days; injunctive relief and fees; no private right of action
laws.exemptions: GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA, small businesses (except sensitive data sale), federal research-law data
laws.research_exemption: Data collected under federal research laws such as the Common Rule is exempt (secondary source)
laws.genetic_data: Sensitive data only when processed to uniquely identify an individual; consent required

laws.law_name: Maryland Online Data Privacy Act of 2024 (MODPA, HB 567)
laws.scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
laws.applies_to: Persons doing business in MD or targeting MD residents that handle data of 35,000+ consumers, or 10,000+ consumers with over 20% of revenue from sale of personal data
laws.key_requirements: Data minimization (collection limited to what is reasonably necessary; sensitive data only when strictly necessary); ban on sale of sensitive data; consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out
laws.data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic and biometric data); minors data
laws.enforcement_authority: Maryland Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
laws.penalties_range: Up to USD 10,000 per violation and USD 25,000 per repeated violation under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act; misdemeanor fine up to USD 1,000 or 1 year prison reported; no private right of action
laws.exemptions: GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA entities, registered national securities associations
laws.genetic_data: Any genetic or biometric data is sensitive data, regardless of identification purpose; processing only if strictly necessary and sale is banned even with consent
laws.notes: Law took effect 2025-10-01 but applies to processing from 2026-04-01; cure period (60 days, if AG finds cure possible) sunsets 2027-04-01

laws.law_name: Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act (HF 4757, Minn. Stat. ch. 325M, secs. 325M.10-325M.21)
laws.scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
laws.applies_to: Entities doing business in MN or targeting MN residents that process data of 100,000+ consumers, or 25,000+ consumers and over 25% of revenue from sale of personal data; small businesses exempt
laws.key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; opt-in consent for sensitive data; data protection assessments
laws.enforcement_authority: Minnesota Attorney General
laws.penalties_range: Civil penalties up to USD 7,500 per violation; no private right of action
laws.exemptions: Banks and credit unions, GLBA data, small businesses (SBA), payment-only transactions (sec. 325M.12)
laws.research_exemption: Internal research to develop or improve products is a permitted purpose (sec. 325M.19); federal human-subjects research entities exempt in the separate genetic law, sec. 325F.995
laws.genetic_data: Sensitive data when processed to uniquely identify an individual (consent required); separate Genetic Information Privacy Act at Minn. Stat. 325F.995
laws.notes: Clifford Chance dates enactment 2024-05-19 (legislature adoption); Walz signature 2024-05-24. HF 2700 (2025) would add consumer health data; in committee

laws.law_name: Rhode Island Data Transparency and Privacy Protection Act (H 7787, R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 6-48.1)
laws.scope: Residents of the state (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
laws.applies_to: Persons doing business in RI or targeting RI residents that process data of 35,000+ consumers, or 10,000+ consumers and over 20% of revenue from sale of personal data; commercial websites and ISPs have disclosure duties
laws.key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out; consent for sensitive data; privacy notice naming third parties; most sources report no cure period
laws.enforcement_authority: Rhode Island Attorney General
laws.penalties_range: Up to USD 10,000 per violation as deceptive trade practice (sources conflict; one lists USD 100-500); no private right of action
laws.exemptions: GLBA, HIPAA and other data-level exemptions including research data
laws.research_exemption: Data-level exemption for research data (scope not confirmed)
laws.genetic_data: Sensitive data requiring opt-in consent only when processed for identification
laws.notes: Enactment date disputed: one source says bill became law without governor signature (transmitted 2024-06-25); cure period sources conflict

laws.law_name: Biometric Information Privacy Act (740 ILCS 14; Public Act 95-994)
laws.jurisdiction: Private right of action in Illinois state circuit court or federal court (740 ILCS 14/20); no regulator
laws.scope: Individuals whose biometric identifiers or information are collected by private entities in Illinois
laws.applies_to: Private entities (not state/local government or Illinois courts)
laws.key_requirements: Written informed consent before collecting biometric data; published retention schedule and destruction guidelines (destroy at end of purpose or within 3 years of last interaction); no sale or profit from biometric data
laws.data_categories: Biometric identifiers (retina/iris scan, fingerprint, voiceprint, hand or face geometry scan) and biometric information
laws.retention_period: Destroy when initial purpose is satisfied or within 3 years of last interaction, whichever is first (sec. 15(a))
laws.enforcement_authority: Aggrieved individuals via courts (private right of action, sec. 20)
laws.penalties_range: Liquidated damages USD 1,000 per negligent violation or USD 5,000 per intentional/reckless violation, or actual damages, plus fees; since Public Act 103-0769 (2024-08-02) counted once per person, not per scan
laws.exemptions: Government agencies and Illinois courts; photographs, signatures, human biological samples used for valid scientific testing or screening, demographic data, physical descriptions
laws.research_exemption: Human biological samples used for valid scientific testing or screening are excluded from biometric identifiers (sec. 10)
laws.genetic_data: Not biometric identifiers when from biological samples for scientific testing; genetic testing is governed by the separate GIPA (410 ILCS 513)
laws.notes: Effective date assumed equal to approval date; no express effective-date text seen. Amended by P.A. 103-0769 (2024-08-02)

laws.law_name: My Health My Data Act (HB 1155, RCW ch. 19.373)
laws.jurisdiction: Washington Attorney General; also private right of action via Consumer Protection Act (RCW 19.86)
laws.scope: Washington consumers and persons whose consumer health data is collected in Washington
laws.applies_to: Regulated entities doing business in WA or targeting WA consumers; small businesses from 2024-06-30
laws.key_requirements: Consumer health data privacy policy; consent for collection and sharing; separate valid authorization for sale; rights of access and deletion; geofencing ban near health facilities
laws.data_categories: Consumer health data (incl. biometric and genetic data)
laws.enforcement_authority: Washington Attorney General and private plaintiffs under the Consumer Protection Act
laws.penalties_range: AG civil penalty up to USD 7,500 per violation (RCW 19.86.140); private treble damages up to USD 25,000 plus fees; violation is per se CPA violation
laws.exemptions: HIPAA PHI, chapter 70.02 RCW records, Common Rule data, 42 CFR Part 2, deidentified data (RCW 19.373.100)
laws.research_exemption: Personal information used for public or peer-reviewed scientific, historical or statistical research in the public interest is not consumer health data; research exemptions in RCW 19.373.100
laws.genetic_data: Genetic and biometric data are expressly consumer health data (full definition text not seen)
laws.notes: Private right of action; first lawsuit filed Feb 2025 per Orrick

laws.law_name: Oklahoma Consumer Data Privacy Act (Senate Bill 546, 2026 Okla. Sess. Laws ch. 8; 75A O.S. ss. 300-320)
laws.scope: Oklahoma residents acting in an individual or household context (not commercial or employment context)
laws.applies_to: Businesses operating in Oklahoma or targeting Oklahoma residents that process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers per year, or at least 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from selling personal data (75A O.S. s. 314(A))
laws.key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale and certain profiling (45-day response plus 45-day extension; appeal process); opt-in consent for sensitive data; privacy notices, data minimization and data protection assessments
laws.data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data used to identify a person, precise geolocation); pseudonymous data
laws.retention_period: No fixed period; collection limited to what is reasonably necessary for disclosed purposes (data minimization); no specific retention schedule found (unconfirmed)
laws.enforcement_authority: Oklahoma Attorney General (exclusive enforcement; no private right of action)
laws.penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $7,500 per violation after a 30-day cure period (non-sunsetting); injunction, attorney fees and investigation costs
laws.exemptions: State agencies and political subdivisions, nonprofits, institutions of higher education, HIPAA covered entities and data, GLBA financial institutions/data; employment and commercial contexts
laws.deceased_data: Not covered in sources found: consumer defined as an Oklahoma natural person acting in an individual or household context; no deceased-person provision found (unconfirmed)
laws.research_exemption: Identifiable private information used in human subjects research is exempt; public-interest research permitted as a common business activity (section number not found)
laws.genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data used to identify a person is sensitive data requiring opt-in consent before processing
laws.notes: Not signed with an official short title per one source; Virginia-style with Texas elements; does not require honoring universal opt-out signals (GPC). Enrolled text on oklegislature.gov was not seen; dates and details come from law-firm summaries. Sources disagree on whether Oklahoma is the 20th or 21st state.

laws.law_name: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act (House Bill 351, Act 2026-552)
laws.scope: Alabama residents (consumers acting in an individual or household context)
laws.applies_to: Persons doing business in Alabama or targeting Alabama residents that process personal data of more than 25,000 consumers (excluding payment-only data) or derive more than 25% of gross revenue from selling personal data; businesses under 500 employees and nonprofits under 100 employees exempt unless they sell data
laws.key_requirements: Consumer rights to confirm, correct, delete and opt out; sensitive data consent; secure channels to exercise rights; Virginia-style model but no mandatory data protection assessments
laws.data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data used to identify an individual)
laws.enforcement_authority: Alabama Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action)
laws.penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $15,000 per violation; 45-day cure period that does not sunset
laws.exemptions: GLBA and HIPAA entities/data, small businesses under 500 employees and nonprofits under 100 employees (if not selling data), human subjects research data, patient safety work product (non-exhaustive list)
laws.research_exemption: Identifiable data used for human subjects research is exempt (section number not found)
laws.genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data used to identify an individual is sensitive data (consent required)
laws.notes: Signing date reported as 2026-04-16 by most sources (FPF, Privacy Daily) and 2026-04-17 by Mayer Brown. Act number 2026-552 comes from a single source (privacylawmap). One local outlet claims effect on 2026-05-01 but others say 2027-05-01 (the latter used). Enrolled text on legislature site not seen.

laws.law_name: Louisiana Data Privacy Act (Senate Bill 386, Act No. 502 of 2026; La. R.S. 51:1780.1-1780.5)
laws.scope: Louisiana residents acting in an individual or household capacity (not commercial or employment context)
laws.applies_to: Persons doing business in Louisiana meeting one of: annual gross revenue over $25 million; buying/selling/sharing personal information of 75,000+ consumers, households or devices; or 50%+ of revenue from selling personal information
laws.key_requirements: Texas-style model: consumer rights (access, correct, delete, port, opt out); consent for sensitive data; data minimization, security and risk assessments
laws.data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic or biometric data)
laws.enforcement_authority: Louisiana Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action)
laws.penalties_range: No penalty schedule in the Act itself; violations are unfair trade practices under LUTPA, civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation (R.S. 51:1407) reported, higher where elderly or disabled persons affected; cure period only 2027-01-01 to 2027-07-31 (30-day notice) (unconfirmed)
laws.exemptions: State agencies and political subdivisions, GLBA financial institutions and data, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, higher education institutions, public utilities; certain research data
laws.research_exemption: Certain research data exempt (exact scope and section not found) (unconfirmed)
laws.genetic_data: Genetic or biometric data included in sensitive data requiring consent
laws.notes: Passed Senate 36-0 and House 94-0; signed 2026-05-29. Enrolled text on legis.la.gov was not seen. Sources disagree on penalty amounts (one cites $10,000 where elderly/disabled are affected) and one lists a private right of action while most exclude it; ranked 22nd state by most sources.

laws.law_name: Vermont Data Privacy and Online Surveillance Act (S.71, Act 145 of 2026; 9 V.S.A. ch. 61A, ss. 2415a-2415k)
laws.scope: Vermont residents (consumers); consumer health data provisions apply regardless of volume thresholds
laws.applies_to: Entities doing business in Vermont or targeting Vermont residents that process personal data of 35,000+ consumers or sensitive data of 3,000+ consumers or sell data of 3,000+ consumers; consumer health data rules apply without thresholds
laws.key_requirements: Connecticut-style model: consumer rights; consent for sensitive data (incl. genetic, biometric, neural, precise geolocation, consumer health, known child data) and limits to what is reasonably necessary; privacy notices must disclose LLM training use; bans manipulative design; no sale or targeted ads for ages 13-17
laws.data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (genetic, biometric, neural, precise geolocation, consumer health data, known child data)
laws.enforcement_authority: Vermont Attorney General (exclusive; no private right of action) under the Vermont Consumer Protection Act
laws.penalties_range: Up to $10,000 per violation under the Consumer Protection Act; discretionary 60-day cure period 2028-01-01 to 2029-06-30
laws.exemptions: Data-level exemptions: various health data, GLBA data, FCRA data, emergency contact information, post-secondary school enrollment/degree verification and related research services
laws.research_exemption: No general research exemption found; only post-secondary school research services data exempt (unconfirmed)
laws.genetic_data: Genetic and biometric data are sensitive data requiring consent before collection and sale; separate H.639 covers direct-to-consumer genetic testing
laws.notes: Legislative record shows signed by Governor 2026-06-16. Sources disagree on state rank (21st/23rd/24th). Separate bill H.639 regulates direct-to-consumer genetic testing (effective 2026-07-01). Enacted text not read; details from law-firm summaries.

laws.law_name: Florida Digital Bill of Rights (CS/CS/SB 262 'Technology Transparency', Ch. 2023-201, Laws of Fla.; Fla. Stat. ss. 501.701 et seq.)
laws.jurisdiction: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Office of the Attorney General)
laws.scope: Florida residents (consumers); narrow controller definition so applies to few businesses
laws.applies_to: Controllers with over $1 billion global gross annual revenue that also derive 50%+ of revenue from online ad sales, operate a consumer smart speaker with voice assistant, or operate an app store with 250,000+ apps; some duties (e.g. sale of sensitive data) reach other for-profit businesses (s. 501.715)
laws.key_requirements: Consumer rights to access, correct, delete, port and opt out of sale, targeted ads and profiling; opt-in consent for sensitive data and its sale; data minimization, security and retention schedule; children's online protections
laws.data_categories: Personal data; sensitive data (incl. genetic data processed to uniquely identify, health diagnoses, precise geolocation)
laws.retention_period: Controllers and processors must adopt and follow a retention schedule; retention ends at the first of several triggers, including two years after the consumer's last interaction
laws.enforcement_authority: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General); no private right of action
laws.penalties_range: Civil penalty up to $50,000 per violation, tripled (up to $150,000) for violations involving a child, failure to delete/correct after verified request, or continued sale/sharing after opt-out; discretionary 45-day cure period (not granted for child-related violations)
laws.exemptions: Entities below the $1 billion/prong thresholds; HIPAA and GLBA entities/data; research and other listed processing purposes (sections not confirmed) (unconfirmed)
laws.research_exemption: Exemption for research purposes reported by one secondary source, section not confirmed (unconfirmed)
laws.genetic_data: Genetic data is sensitive data only when processed to uniquely identify an individual; sale of sensitive data requires consent
laws.notes: Limited-scope law; counted as a comprehensive privacy law by some sources and not by others. Enforcement rule Fla. Admin. Code 2-3.003 effective 2024-07-18. AG sued Roku under the Act in 2025 (reported settled 2026-06). No 2026 amendments found.

laws.jurisdiction: Regulatory and Control Unit for Personal Data (URCDP)
laws.key_requirements: Prior informed consent, purpose limitation, data subject rights, database registration
laws.retention_period: As long as necessary for the purpose
laws.enforcement_authority: Regulatory and Control Unit for Personal Data (URCDP) within AGESIC
laws.penalties_range: Up to 500,000 Indexed Units (UI) fine
laws.exemptions: Personal/domestic use; public security, defence & State security
laws.notes: Regulated by Decree 414/009; territorial scope extended by Law 19.670 (arts 37-40)

laws.law_name: Law on Personal Data (ZRU-547)
laws.applies_to: Public & private owners and operators of personal databases

laws.retention_period: Art. 10: storage period determined by date purposes of collection/processing are achieved; identifiable only as purposes require; destroy when purpose met
laws.enforcement_authority: Personalization Agency under the Ministry of Justice
laws.penalties_range: Administrative fines up to 50 base values; criminal liability for repeat offences
laws.exemptions: Household use; state secrets; defence & national security information
laws.notes: Localization rule (2021) narrowed by Mar 2026 amendment; adequacy list of 49 countries set Jul 2026
